Name: Golgotha
Goal: Drop down a hole or shaft into a lower level
What it is there: The first story dungeon: a slimy sewer entered by jumping down a shaft.
Why it fits: Qud's first dungeon: a slime-choked sewer you enter by jumping down a slimy shaft. Dropping down a level is something nearly every dungeon game asks of you, so it suits a Low location.

Name: Bethesda Susa
Goal: Reach a frozen area
What it is there: A frozen hospital dungeon that gets colder each stratum, down to -110°.
Why it fits: A mid-game dungeon that gets colder every stratum, down to -110° in the cryobarrios. Reaching the cold is the whole shape of the place. `ice` has one body today, so this would also be a reason to add more.

Name: Tomb of the Eaters
Goal: Enter a tomb, crypt or catacomb
What it is there: The largest dungeon in the game, 100+ zones of sultans' tombs around the Spindle.
Why it fits: Qud's largest dungeon, over 100 zones of sultan tombs around the Spindle. A tomb is common across games and `undead` is the second most common enemy tag, so it suits a High location with a big payout.

Name: Becoming Nook
Description: A machine that installs, upgrades and removes cybernetics. It calls everyone who uses it 'Aristocrat'.
Choices: Install: lose 1 Max Health, gain a random relic | Upgrade: spend 3 Gold, Gain +1 Max Health | Uninstall: lose a relic, Gain +2 Max Health | Leave
Why it fits: Objects here are machines you stand at and choose from (the arcade machines). A nook trades body for chrome, which is Max Health against relics here, and each choice can be undone the way Qud's can.

Name: Sokoban
Goal: Solve a puzzle room
What it is there: A branch of four boulder-pushing puzzle levels, modelled on the Japanese game; the top holds a bag of holding or an amulet of reflection.
Why it fits: Puzzle rooms appear in a great many games, and it carries NetHack's best-known prize.

Name: Gnomish Mines
Goal: Reach the bottom of a mine
What it is there: A branch of open cave levels full of gnomes, dwarves and hill orcs, with Minetown partway down.
Why it fits: Mines and caves are everywhere in these games; the gnomes, dwarves and hill orcs that fill it are the goblin tag's natural home.

Name: Fort Ludios
Goal: Find a hidden vault
What it is there: A hidden fortress reached through a portal in a vault; a garrison of soldiers guards Croesus and his treasury.
Why it fits: A secret vault full of treasure guarded by an army: a High location with a big payout, as Ludios is.

Name: Fountain
Description: A fountain of uncertain water.
Choices: Quaff: small chance of a wish (gain a Rare relic); otherwise water moccasins (spawn an enemy) or a nymph steals 1 Gold | Dip a Weapon: may become Excalibur | Leave
What it is there: Quaff from it (wishes, water moccasins, a water nymph who steals, a water demon), dip items in it (Excalibur), or dig it up.
Why it fits: Objects here are things you stand at and choose from; a fountain's gamble is as old as the genre, and dipping links it to Excalibur.

Name: Throne
Description: An empty throne in a hall of sleeping courtiers.
Choices: Sit: one random effect: Gain +1 to a stat, identify all your loot, gain a Rare relic, the court wakes (spawn 2 enemies), lose Gold, or lose 2 Health; the throne may vanish | Leave
What it is there: Sit on it for one of a dozen effects: gain a stat, identify everything, a wish, genocide, summon the throne room's court, lose gold, an electric shock; the throne may vanish.
Why it fits: A random effect for the brave, and a second gamble object beside the arcade machines.

Name: Sink
Description: A kitchen sink, oddly far underground.
Choices: Kick: a Black Pudding climbs out (spawn an enemy) or you find a random loot | Drop a loot down the drain: lose it, and learn whether it was positive or negative | Leave
What it is there: Kick it for a black pudding, a 'dish washer' or a hidden ring; drop a ring down the drain to learn what it was and lose it.
Why it fits: Identifying loot by throwing it away is a cost the identify gamble here can actually show; the kick results are pure NetHack.

Name: Altar
Description: An altar to an unknown god.
Choices: Drop your loot on it: learn whether each piece is positive or negative | Sacrifice: lose 1 Health, chance of a Rare weapon | Pray: heal 2 if under half Health, otherwise lose 1 Luck | Leave
What it is there: Drop items on it to see whether they are blessed, uncursed or cursed; sacrifice fresh corpses for gifts; pray for help.
Why it fits: Learning whether loot is good or bad is the identify system's whole question, and the altar answers it without spending a scroll.

Name: Izchak
Description: Sells light: candles and lamps.
Choices: Stock a candle or lamp on the shelf | Steal: take an item without paying, and the Keystone Kops stand up on the board
What it is there: Minetown's lighting-shop keeper, named in memory of NetHack developer Izchak Miller; every shopkeeper sends the Keystone Kops after a thief.
Why it fits: Named shopkeepers are planned (spec §14.5); Izchak is the most famous shopkeeper in roguelikes, and his Kops give stealing a cost.
Builds on: ShopPanel2 shopkeeper field, Keystone Kops (goal candidate)
Needs: new: leaving a shop without paying

Name: Ziggurat
Goal: Clear 3 floors in a row without leaving
What it is there: The most dangerous and lucrative branch: 27 floors of one monster theme each, growing in size and treasure, with no way back up.
Why it fits: The genre's endurance test: a goal of floors in a row, at a High tier with a big payout, as a ziggurat pays.

Name: Trove
Goal: Pay to open a locked treasure room
What it is there: A one-off portal full of themed treasure that charges a toll to enter: gold, an item of a kind, or a rune.
Why it fits: The only location idea here that asks you to pay to get in, which turns gold into a different kind of reward.
Needs: new: a location with an entry cost

Name: Slime Pits
Goal: Reach the bottom of a slime- or acid-filled area
What it is there: A five-floor branch of acidic walls and amorphous horrors, with the Royal Jelly and a treasure vault at the bottom.
Why it fits: Acid and ooze are a theme of half the dungeon games here, and the slime tag gives it bodies to favour.

Name: Tristram
Goal: Talk to everyone in a town
What it is there: The small town above the cathedral: Griswold, Adria, Pepin, Ogden, Wirt, Cain and Farnham, each with something to sell or say.
Why it fits: The genre's archetypal town. Talking your way round a hub is something most games with a town offer.

Name: King Leoric's Tomb
Goal: Pull a lever that opens a sealed room
What it is there: The Skeleton King's tomb off level 3, sealed until you pull a lever.
Why it fits: Pulling a lever to open a sealed room is a staple of dungeon games, and the tomb is full of skeletons for the tag.

Name: Goat Shrine
Description: A shrine of goat-horned figures.
Choices: Pray: one random effect: Gain +1 to a stat, identify all your loot, heal to full, or a curse (lose 1 Max Health) | Leave
What it is there: One of Diablo's shrines: a random shrine effect, which may be beneficial or a permanent curse.
Why it fits: A one-use gamble object, as every Diablo shrine is; good or cursed, you don't know until you pray.
Clones: Altar of Chaos (Red Rogue): pray to RNG, the God of Chaos, for one of thirteen miracles, from a free item or a level to a Horror or a polymorph

Name: Fountain of Tears
Description: Water that runs like tears.
Choices: Drink: lose 1 of a random verb or stat, gain 1 of another | Leave
What it is there: A Diablo fountain: -1 to one random attribute, +1 to another.
Why it fits: A trade between two stats, the one shrine that is neither good nor bad.

Name: Griswold
Description: Weapons and armour, and repairs.
Choices: Shelf leans to weapons | Repair: restore a weapon's charge for 1 Gold
What it is there: Tristram's blacksmith: buys and sells weapons and armour, repairs gear, and forges Griswold's Edge from the Anvil of Fury. 'Well, what kin I do fer ya?'
Why it fits: Named shopkeepers are planned (spec §14.5), and Tristram's four are the genre's template. The blacksmith sells and repairs weapons.

Name: Adria
Description: Potions, scrolls and wands.
Choices: Shelf leans to potions, scrolls and wands | Recharge: refill a wand for 1 Gold
What it is there: Tristram's witch: sells potions, scrolls, books, staves and recharges them. 'I sense a soul in search of answers.'
Why it fits: The witch sells the magic: the shelf's potions, scrolls and wands, which the plan says shops should also stock.
Builds on: ShopPanel2 shopkeeper field, potions, scrolls, wands
Needs: new: shelves with consumables (spec §14.5)

Name: Wirt
Description: One rare item. Looking costs extra.
Choices: Pay 1 Gold to look: one Rare item at +2 Gold
What it is there: The peg-legged boy who charges 50 gold just to see his one item, always a rare one, at a steep price.
Why it fits: A shop with a catch: pay to look. A different shape of shop from the other two.
Needs: new: a fee to see the shelf

Name: Pepin
Description: Healing.
Choices: Heal 1 Health for free once per visit | Shelf leans to healing potions
What it is there: Tristram's healer: heals you for free and sells healing potions and elixirs.
Why it fits: A healer who sells the thing the plan names as missing: health (spec §14.5).
Needs: new: health on the shelf (spec §14.5)

Name: Ruins
Goal: Explore ruins of a lost civilisation
What it is there: The remains of an ancient civilisation below the Caves: clockwork monsters, the Labyrinth and the Ancient Guardian.
Why it fits: Ancient ruins beneath the world are in countless games; exploring them is a High Discovery with a big payout.

Name: Crock Pot
Description: A pot over hot coals.
Choices: Cook: lose 2 food loot, gain a cooked dish (heals 3, or +1 Max Health) | Leave
What it is there: A structure that cooks four ingredients into a dish worth more than its parts.
Why it fits: The food family (9 pieces) has nothing to spend food on; cooking two pieces into a dish is Don't Starve's whole kitchen.
Needs: new: combining loot into new loot

Name: Spiky Cactus
Description: Can't be moved. An enemy pushed into it or walking into it takes 1 damage. Leaves Water when destroyed.
What it is there: An inanimate desert object with Thorns: it can't be moved, gives Thorns to what touches it, and leaves Water when broken.
Why it fits: A unit that only hurts what touches it is a different job from the Landmine, which goes off once.
Builds on: Landmine unit, Push (pushing an enemy into it)
Needs: new: a Thorns unit

Name: Decoy
Description: Enemies in its row attack it instead of you. Explodes when destroyed: 1 damage to everything next to it.
What it is there: A static robot object from Spawn Decoy: it can't move or attack, enemies may attack it, and it explodes when destroyed.
Why it fits: The board has nothing that draws attacks away from the hero; a decoy is the cheapest way to buy a turn.
Needs: new: a unit enemies attack instead of you

Name: Tesla Coil
Description: Each turn, zaps a random body within 3 squares for 1 damage, with a small chance to Stun it.
What it is there: A static robot familiar that zaps a random unit within 3 tiles for 3 Electric damage each turn, with a 10% chance to Stun.
Why it fits: A unit that acts on its own each turn; the Landmine only reacts.
Needs: new: a unit that acts every turn

Name: Tombstone
Description: Stands up a 1-Health undead body at the end of every turn until it is destroyed (1 Health, bombable).
What it is there: A Boneyard object: the Zombie variant summons a Zombie Cat at the end of each round; the Ghost variant may release a ghost and coins when destroyed.
Why it fits: An enemy-side unit: a hazard the player has to clear before it fills the board.
Needs: new: a unit on the enemies' side

Name: Gas Cloud
Description: Poisons whatever moves through it; lasts 2 turns. Fire on it makes it explode.
What it is there: An object on its own gas layer: poisons units moving through it, disappears after 2 turns or when crossed, and explodes when Fire touches it.
Why it fits: A Poison tile; poison is common across the source games and missing here, and it chains with the Fire tile.
Needs: new: Poison (status) and a gas tile

Name: Tar
Description: Applies Tarred to whatever stands in it. If Fire reaches it, it burns.
What it is there: Tar from the Spewer's pills and Tar Babies inflicts Tarred, which Fire turns into Burn.
Why it fits: A tile that sets up the Fire tile: slow them in tar, then light it.
Needs: new: a Tar tile

Name: Slot Machine
Description: A one-armed bandit, humming.
Choices: Pay 1 Gold: spin for a random pickup (Gold, a bomb, a key, Health), a fly enemy, or nothing | Bomb it: it explodes and drops a few pickups, then it's gone | Leave
What it is there: Isaac's slot machine: bump it to spend a penny and spin; it may pay out pickups, a fly, or a prize, and blows up when bombed. Also in Mewgenics (same studio), where it drops pickups when hit and explodes with fire.
Why it fits: A third arcade machine: objects here are machines with choices, and the arcade tag already groups two Isaac machines.
Builds on: arcade tag (Blood Donation Machine, Donation Machine)

Name: Key Master
Description: A hooded beggar jingling a ring of empty hooks.
Choices: Give a Key: chance of a chest, keys back, or a Rare relic (then he leaves) | Leave
What it is there: A beggar who takes keys; each donation may drop pickups, and sometimes he leaves an item and vanishes. One of eight beggars, each wanting a different donation.
Why it fits: The first thing that SPENDS keys. Keys have nothing to open yet (spec §4), and a beggar who takes them is the simplest use.

Name: Fortune Telling Machine
Description: A fortune teller in a glass box.
Choices: Pay 1 Gold: a fortune (nothing), or a random card, a trinket or +1 Shield | Leave
What it is there: Spend a penny: it prints a fortune, or pays out a tarot card, a trinket or a soul heart.
Why it fits: Isaac's other machine, and a cheap way to hand out a card or a soul heart.

Name: Secret Room
Goal: Find a secret room by blowing open a wall
What it is there: Rooms hidden behind walls, found by bombing a wall next to them; Super Secret Rooms hide at dead ends.
Why it fits: Bombing a wall to find a hidden room is a staple of action roguelikes, and it gives bombs a use on the map side.

Name: Sacrifice Room
Goal: Hurt yourself on purpose 3 times for a reward
What it is there: A room with spikes in the middle: hurt yourself on them for a chance at chests and other rewards.
Why it fits: Hurting yourself for a reward is a goal the self-damage relics (IV Bag, Piggy Bank) already like.

Name: Challenge Room
Goal: Survive an ambush you started at full health
What it is there: A room that only opens if Isaac's health is full; inside, waves of enemies (or bosses) for extra rewards.
Why it fits: An ambush you can only open at full health: a goal with an entry condition.

Name: Locked Display Cabinet
Description: A dusty cabinet behind cracked glass, locked.
Choices: Use a Key: take what's inside (a Rare loot) | Break the glass: a random loot, but lose 1 Health | Leave
What it is there: A curio in the Ruins: use a Skeleton Key on it for its treasure; forcing it risks a trap.
Why it fits: A second thing that spends keys, and a curio with a better outcome for using the right provision.

Name: Confession Booth
Description: A booth with a curtain, and someone breathing behind it.
Choices: Confess: heal 2, or gain a random Debuff | Use Holy Water: heal 3 | Leave
What it is there: A curio in the Ruins: pray at it for stress relief or a quirk; Holy Water makes the good outcome certain.
Why it fits: A curio that can heal or hurt depending on what you bring, the shape every Darkest Dungeon curio has.

Name: Nomad Wagon
Description: Trinkets, idols and lucky charms.
Choices: Shelf of three trinkets | Upgrade: pay 2 Gold for a fourth slot this run
What it is there: The Hamlet's trinket merchant, whose stock refreshes each week; upgrades widen the stock and lower prices.
Why it fits: A shop that only sells trinkets: the shelf here sells relics and loot mixed, and a trinket stall is a different shop.

Name: Cove
Goal: Defeat 3 creatures from the sea
What it is there: The second-to-last dungeon: a water-logged smuggler's cove full of pelagic horrors, where the Siren and the Drowned Crew wait.
Why it fits: A sea-cave location gives the fish tag (3 bodies) somewhere to belong.

Name: Weald
Goal: Clear a path through an overgrown forest
What it is there: The second dungeon: woods overrun by an unnatural fungal infestation, home of the Hag.
Why it fits: A fungus-infested forest suits the mushroom tag, and forests are everywhere.

Name: Gas Station Siege
Goal: Hold a building against a horde until it lets up
What it is there: A looting location: an untouched gas station with a horde close by. Looting it means getting stuck in a siege until it's over.
Why it fits: Death Road's sieges (hold out for a set time) are a goal any horde or survival game can host, and the undead tag has bodies to send.

Name: Magma
Description: Destroys any body that enters it, unless it is Fireproof. Defeated this way it pays nothing.
What it is there: Red-hot molten rock from deep underground; anything that falls in burns. 'Magma is very Fun.'
Why it fits: The deadliest tile possible: the board has nothing that simply removes a body, except bombs.
Needs: new: a Magma tile

Name: Cage Trap
Description: An enemy that steps on it is caught: taken off the board, with no drop and no gold. One use.
What it is there: A trap of one mechanism and a cage; whatever walks onto its tile is caught alive.
Why it fits: A trap that removes a body alive: it's gone, but it pays nothing, unlike a goal.
Needs: new: a unit that removes a body

Name: Hidden Fun Stuff
Goal: Dig deeper than you were meant to
What it is there: The Underworld below the magma sea, reached by breaching a hollow adamantine vein: the demons of the 'eerie glowing pit' pour out.
Why it fits: Digging too deep is a story every roguelike player knows; a High location with a big payout and a big risk.

Name: Dwarven Caravan
Description: Trades goods for goods.
Choices: Barter: swap one of your loot for one on the shelf | Leave
What it is there: Merchant caravans from the Mountainhome and friendly civilisations arrive through the year to trade goods for goods.
Why it fits: A shop that barters instead of selling: swapping a piece for a piece is a different shape of shop.
Needs: new: bartering a loot for a loot

Name: Silk Cradle
Goal: Make your way through a cave full of webs
What it is there: The fourth biome, ruled by Shamura: a cave full of spider webs, spiders and the bones of what they caught.
Why it fits: A web-filled cave suits the spider tag (4 bodies) and the Web tile.

Name: Rakshasa
Description: Food.
Choices: Shelf of three food pieces
What it is there: A mantis-shrimp chef who runs a restaurant in the dungeons, offering three kinds of food.
Why it fits: A shop that only sells food, which the food family (9 pieces) has nothing like.

Name: Healing Pool
Description: A still pool, glowing faintly.
Choices: Bathe: heal up to 2 Health; it holds 4 in total this run, then goes dark | Leave
What it is there: A special room on each dungeon floor whose pool heals Will, up to a set amount per floor; the water darkens as it's used up.
Why it fits: An object that runs dry: it heals, but only so much in a whole run.
Needs: new: an object with a limited supply
Clones: Autodoc (Quasimorph): a field station that heals 60 HP or every wound for a charge of batteries, and stops working if it is damaged

Name: Edward
Description: Banking. "Trust your money in my hands and I will make it grow before your eyes."
Choices: Invest: deposit Gold, which gains or loses 1 each game | Cash out: take it all back
What it is there: The Banker: invest gold on a Sunday and watch it grow (or shrink) each day; cash out any time.
Why it fits: A shop that grows your money instead of selling anything: the Donation Machine's bank, as a person.

Name: Holy Mountain
Goal: Reach a safe haven between two areas
What it is there: The sanctuary between each of Noita's biomes: it heals you fully, holds a shop and a perk altar, and Stevari guards it.
Why it fits: A location whose payout is rest rather than loot: arriving safe is the reward.

Name: Perk Altar
Description: Three glowing perks rest on an altar.
Choices: Take one: gain one of three random relics | Reroll: pay 1 Gold (2, then 4…) for three new ones | Leave
What it is there: At the exit of each Holy Mountain: three perks, take one and the others vanish; a reroll machine re-deals them for a cost that doubles each time.
Why it fits: A pick-one-of-three that you can pay to reroll, at a price that climbs: chests have no reroll.
Needs: new: a reroll with a rising price

Name: Shimmering Caverns
Goal: Break 5 crystals or gems
Description: A crystal labyrinth that rings when anything goes off.
What it is there: A crystalline labyrinth: Shatter Rocks burst into shards when a bomb goes off, and Prism Stones split projectiles four ways.
Why it fits: A cave full of crystal is a common place in games, and breaking the crystals is what it's for.

Name: Delvemore Dungeon
Goal: Free a prisoner from a cell
Description: A flooded castle dungeon. Somebody is locked in down here.
What it is there: The castle dungeon under the Goldmine, where Lillyth is locked in a cell behind a Master's Key and the Gargoyles guard the key.
Why it fits: UnderMine's helpers are found locked up (Wayland behind a wall, Dodson and Lillyth in cells); a prison break is a common side job.

Name: Cursed Chest
Description: A chest with a purple lock. It opens for free.
Choices: Open it: Gain +1 Small Chest and a random curse | Leave
What it is there: A chest with a purple lock that opens for free and gives you a curse with its loot.
Why it fits: A chest with a price that isn't Gold: there are 3 curses in the game and nothing that hands them out in exchange for loot.

Name: Shatter Rock
Description: Turns orange, then red, each time a bomb goes off on the board. The third time, or when bombed, it shatters: 1 damage to the first body in each of the 8 directions.
What it is there: Caverns rocks with three states (green, orange, red) that change whenever an explosion goes off in the room; destroyed, they fire crystal shards in all 8 directions.
Why it fits: A unit that reacts to bombs: it chains off them rather than going off once, like the Landmine does.
Needs: new: a unit that counts explosions

Name: Sho'guul
Description: Legendary relics. The price is curses.
Choices: Shelf of three Legendary relics, each costing 2 random curses; take one and the others vanish | Leave
What it is there: The Opulent Demon, behind a mouth-shaped portal: sells only legendary relics, each priced at 2 or more curses; taking one destroys the rest.
Why it fits: A shop priced in curses: a different currency from every other shopkeeper, and the board's curses are thin.
Needs: new: a price in curses

Name: Dibble
Description: Bombs, keys and potions, cheap. The door takes 2 keys.
Choices: Pay 2 Keys to enter: Bombs and Keys at half price | Leave
What it is there: Dibble's Emporium in the Delvemore Dungeon costs 2 keys to enter, and sells a Key Ring and a Bag O' Bombs at half price; later he sells bombs, keys and potions.
Why it fits: Nothing spends a key yet (inventory: keys); a shop with a key on the door gives them a use.
Needs: new: a shop that costs keys to enter; bombs and keys on the shelf

Name: Goblin Warren
Goal: Defeat a goblin war band and its leader
Description: Brown mud walls and a doorway of hanging skins. It smells.
What it is there: Mud-walled warrens of small rooms under a goblin warlord, home to goblins, conjurers, mystics, totems and jackals, with one doorway of hanging skins and a hoard of weapons and armour.
Why it fits: A themed area full of one enemy kind, with a boss in the back: the board's tags make that a goal.

Name: Commutation Altar
Description: Crude diagrams on this altar and its twin invite you to place items upon them.
Choices: Place two pieces: they swap their enchantments (once) | Leave
What it is there: Twin altars on depths 13-26: place two items and their enchantment levels swap, once.
Why it fits: A one-time trade between two pieces you already own: nothing else in the game moves value from one piece to another.
Needs: new: enchanted pieces

Name: Lichen
Description: Can't move or attack. A body that starts its turn next to it is poisoned. Every 3 turns it grows onto an empty tile next to it.
What it is there: Deadly red lichen, from a potion of creeping death or infested monsters: it poisons anything standing on it, monsters won't cross it, and it grows to a neighbouring square about every 10 turns.
Why it fits: A unit that spreads: the board has nothing that grows by itself.
Builds on: Gas Cloud and Blight (candidates, for poison)
Needs: new: a unit that spreads; Poison

Name: Bloodwort
Description: Hit it to burst a pod: you heal 2, and so does every enemy next to it. Three pods.
What it is there: An impassable plant whose seed pods, walked into or burned, release a cloud of healing gas that heals you, your allies and any enemies in it.
Why it fits: Healing on the board, with a catch: it heals whoever is next to it, enemies too.
Needs: new: a unit that heals everything near it

Name: Dewar
Description: When hit, it shatters: Gas Cloud on its tile and the 8 around it.
What it is there: Glass containers of extremely pressurised gas (caustic, paralytic, confusion or methane); struck, one shatters and floods the area with twenty potions' worth of gas.
Why it fits: A unit to set off on purpose: break it near the enemies, not near you.

Name: Prisoners' Quarters
Goal: Escape from a prison
Description: A cell, a dead knight and a door. Out is the only direction.
What it is there: The first biome: the Beheaded wakes in a cell, takes a weapon off the Tutorial Knight's corpse and starts fighting its way out of the island's prison.
Why it fits: Dead Cells starts in a cell and the whole game is a prison break; many games open the same way.

Name: Timed Door
Description: A door with a clock over it. It's still open, for now.
Choices: If you've played 5 games or fewer this run: open it, Gain +1 Medium Chest | Otherwise it's shut
What it is there: Doors at the end of early biomes that stay open only if you arrive within a time limit, with treasure and cells behind; opening one is an achievement.
Why it fits: A reward for speed: nothing on the map cares how quickly you got there.
Needs: new: an object that checks how many games you've played

Name: Commencement
Goal: Win a fight after an enemy has taken all your items
Description: The moon. Something up there wants your things.
What it is there: The final stage, the moon of Petrichor V, where Mithrix waits at the apex; reached through the Primordial Teleporter.
Why it fits: On Commencement, Mithrix's last phase strips you of every item and you fight for them back; few fights ask you to win with nothing. ('Go to a Moon' is already a live goal, so the moon itself couldn't be the goal.)

Name: Shrine of the Mountain
Description: A stone shrine with a mountain carved on it.
Choices: Pray: the next boss stands up with a second boss beside it, and its chest is doubled | Leave
What it is there: Activating it makes the stage's Teleporter Event harder (extra bosses, Elite bosses) and adds another copy of each item the teleporter drops; several stack.
Why it fits: A challenge you choose to take: a harder boss for a bigger chest. Nothing on the map lets you raise the stakes.
Clones: Paragon Relic (Caveblazers): a relic that makes every boss of the run deal double damage with 50% more health and new attacks, for greater rewards

Name: Shrine of Order
Description: A shrine of perfect order. It wants your things to match.
Choices: Pay 1 Gold: for each rarity, every piece of that rarity becomes one of them, picked at random | Leave
What it is there: A rare shrine: pay a Lunar Coin and, for each rarity, one of your items is picked at random and every other item of that rarity becomes it.
Why it fits: The most dramatic thing an object could do to the pack: collapse every rarity into one piece.
Needs: new: turning pieces into copies of one

Name: Void Cradle
Description: A purple cradle, humming.
Choices: Open it: Lose half your Health; Gain a Rare item; 50% chance a body stands up on the board | Leave
What it is there: An interactable that costs half your health to open, gives a void item, and may release up to four Void Infestors.
Why it fits: A chest paid for in Health, with a body or two in it.

Name: Newt
Description: Lunar pieces, for Lunar Coins. Time stands still in here.
Choices: Shelf of three lunar pieces, priced in Lunar Coins | Trade a piece for one of the next rarity up | Leave
What it is there: The Bazaar Between Time, reached by a Blue Portal or by paying a Newt Altar: sells items for Lunar Coins, which carry over between runs, and trades items up in two crucibles.
Why it fits: The shop that sells lunar pieces: each one strong with a real downside, and priced in something other than Gold.
Builds on: ShopPanel2 shopkeeper field, the lunar tag (candidates)
Needs: new: a currency kept between runs

Name: Fallen Angel Shrine
Description: A shrine to a fallen Bullet Angel.
Choices: Sacrifice a heart: Lose 1 Max Health; Gain +1 Strength for the rest of the run and a random curse | Leave
What it is there: Sacrifice a heart container (two as the Robot) for +25% damage, and take 1.5 Curse.
Why it fits: Strength for Max Health with a curse on top: the curses here have no shrine to come from.

Name: Lock-a-doora
Description: A big grey lock with a face. It looks smug.
Choices: Use a Key: it dies; Gain +1 Medium Chest | No key: it laughs and spits at you
What it is there: Large sentient grey locks on doorways and Mini-Reward Room vaults; a Key opens one and kills it. Try it without a key and it laughs and spits at you.
Why it fits: Something that takes a key: nothing spends one yet (inventory: keys).
Needs: new: spending a key

Name: Cursula
Description: Magic items, half price. The other half is a curse.
Choices: Shelf at half price; each purchase adds a random curse | Leave
What it is there: A merchant of magic items, charming guns and heart containers, all at 50% off; every purchase adds 2.5 Curse on top of the item's own.
Why it fits: Half price, paid for in curses as well as Gold: a different deal from Sho'guul, who takes only curses.

Name: Flynt
Description: Locks, keys and chests, for keys.
Choices: Shelf of key, chest and lock pieces priced in Keys (1 for most, 2-3 for the best) | Leave
What it is there: Sells key, chest and lock themed items and guns for Keys: 1 for D-B tier, 2 for A, 3 for S. 'When you unlock a door in the Gungeon, they... go to a better place. I hope.'
Why it fits: The only Gungeon merchant paid in keys, which gives keys a use here.
Needs: new: a price in keys

Name: Black Powder Mine
Goal: Ride a minecart
Description: Mineshafts, rails and acid.
What it is there: The third chamber: caverns and mineshafts where gunpowder is dug, with minecart tracks winding through and lakes of acid.
Why it fits: Mine carts are a staple of mine levels, and riding one is something to do in them.

Name: Bullet Hell
Goal: Go to hell
Description: Candles, chains and screaming bullets. Very warm.
What it is there: The secret sixth chamber, an infernal cavern of candles, chains and burning skeletons, which opens only after the pasts of all four main Gungeoneers are killed.
Why it fits: Going to hell is a late, hard, famous destination in games, and Gungeon's is sealed until you've earned it.

Name: Frog Trap
Description: A body that enters or starts its turn on this tile becomes Frog for 2 turns
What it is there: A hidden trap in the Monster Tower; whatever steps on it, Koh or monster, turns into a Lazy Frog for a while. Only Koh can disarm traps, by attacking them from the next tile.
Why it fits: A tile that changes what a body is, not just how hurt it is.

Name: Soap
Description: A body that enters this tile slides one more tile in the same direction
What it is there: The Slippery ailment, from bubble bombs, soap shields and bath bombs: you slide after you stop running, and Slippery monsters slip and slide around too.
Why it fits: A tile that moves bodies: pushed onto it, they keep going, which makes Push a combo.
Needs: new: a tile that slides a body

Name: Sunken Library
Goal: Find a lost library
Description: Golden domes, half buried in sand. Something larger lies dormant underneath.
What it is there: Golden domes poking out of the desert sand: rappel down and fight the Lorekeeper, ten Phylacteries and the Ancient Honor Guard for the Black Book.
Why it fits: Lost libraries are a fixture of dungeon games, and this one is buried in sand and guarded by its keeper.

Name: Grotesque Tree
Description: A slender tree. Something about it is off.
Choices: Take a little: Gain a random potion | Drink it all: nothing happens | Leave
What it is there: A slender tree in a forest clearing that seems off: take a little and you get a water skin; drink it all and you get nothing.
Why it fits: An object whose greedy choice is a joke at your expense.

Name: Kali Altar
Description: A bloodstained altar to Kali.
Choices: Offer what you defeated last game: 4 or more, Gain a random item; 8 or more, Gain a Kapala | Smash it: Gain +2 Gold and a random curse | Leave
What it is there: Bloodstained altars to the fickle goddess Kali: lay stunned or dead bodies on one for favour, which pays out in items and health at thresholds. Destroy one and Kali's anger brings punishments.
Why it fits: An altar that takes bodies, not items or Gold: the board's defeated enemies get a second use.
Needs: new: an object that counts what you've defeated

Name: Black Market
Goal: Find a hidden shop
Description: Behind a wall that sounds hollow, a market that isn't on any map.
What it is there: A secret level off the Jungle's first three levels, behind a ground tile you blow or dig open, with seven shops; the only place to buy the Ankh. The Udjat Eye blinks faster as you near it.
Why it fits: A hidden shop is a classic secret, and this one is a whole street of them.

Name: City of Gold
Goal: Find a city of gold
Description: Gold walls, gold floors. The door only opens for those who carried everything here.
What it is there: A secret level in the Temple, behind a Golden Door, reached only by collecting the Udjat Eye, the Ankh, the Hedjet and the Scepter in one run; the Book of the Dead found there leads on to Hell.
Why it fits: A secret level reached by carrying a chain of artifacts through a whole run: the hardest Discovery a game can offer.

Name: Fairy Chest
Description: A glowing chest. A sign over it sets a condition.
Choices: Take its challenge: your next game carries a random restriction (no damage, defeat everything, or be quick); meet it: Gain +1 Large Chest | Leave
What it is there: A chest in a challenge room that opens only once its objective is met (take no damage, defeat everything, reach it in time...); fail and that heir can never open it. It holds runes, then stat upgrades.
Why it fits: A chest you earn by playing a certain way: the restriction is the price.

Name: Infernal Trove
Description: A chest of the Underworld. The moment you touch it, shades rise around it.
Choices: Open it: 3 bodies stand up; defeat them within 2 turns, Gain +1 Large Chest, or later, +1 Small Chest | Leave it
What it is there: Treasure chests that summon enemies when you try to open them; the reward decays as the fight goes on, and freezes when the last one dies.
Why it fits: A chest that pays more the faster you clear what guards it: speed as a reward on the board.
Needs: new: a reward that shrinks with turns
Clones: Battle Totem (Muck): activate it and three enemies stand up, and beating them pays a powerup

Name: Creature Den
Goal: Beat two waves of enemies without healing in between
Description: Bones and fur in the mouth of a cave. Something in there has a litter.
What it is there: A DD2 combat node, guaranteed in the Foetor and the Tangle: eight Creatures in two waves, with no heal and no cooldown reset between them.
Why it fits: Two waves back to back with no healing in between is the den's whole difficulty, and plenty of games chain fights that way.

Name: Oasis
Description: Clear water in the middle of the ruin, and nobody drinking it.
Choices: Drink: heal 2 | Fill a flask: Gain a random potion | Leave
What it is there: A node, 'a sanctum of tranquility': mostly stress heals, and one option fills a flask with Mineral-Rich Spring Water, a strong combat item.
Why it fits: A rest stop with one useful choice, the way DD2 offers one option per hero.

Name: The Hoarder
Description: A hunched old man and a cart of everything. He seems to be somewhere else as well.
Choices: Shelf of four pieces of any kind | One trinket no other shop sells
What it is there: A shop node selling combat items, inn items, stagecoach items and trinkets, some only he sells. 'His attention is unfocused. As if he is in two places at once.' Heavily implied to be the first game's Caretaker.
Why it fits: A shop that carries a bit of everything, with stock only he has; the old Caretaker, gone strange.
Needs: new: shop-only trinkets

Name: Gauntlet
Goal: Clear a timed challenge room
Description: An empty room. When you try to leave, a large hermit steps out and asks you to come closer.
What it is there: A run's hidden set of six timed challenge rooms, the last a boss, run by Ace, who stops you leaving the empty room it hides behind.
Why it fits: Every room in it has a clock, and the room stops the moment you are hit: a timed challenge is the whole place.

Name: Breachstone
Description: A black stake in the floor, like a grave marker. The air around it is thin.
Choices: Break it: 2 bodies stand up, and your Weapons can't swing until they fall; defeat them, Gain +1 Large Chest | Leave
What it is there: A gravestone-like stake; destroy it and a breach opens, a harder room where your weapon is locked away and you fight with your ship's basic gun.
Why it fits: An optional fight you take with one hand tied, for the reward.
Needs: new: weapons locked while bodies stand

Name: Kleines
Description: A cat behind a crate counter. 'Point it at somebody you don't like, hold fire and lean back.'
Choices: Shelf of three Weapons
What it is there: A good-humoured cat who sells unlocks from a makeshift shop in the Hub, with a tip for every weapon.
Why it fits: A cat with a shop: cat is the biggest enemy tag in the game (11 bodies), and a weapons dealer suits a weapons game.

Name: Imp Shrine
Description: A small shrine with an imp on top, grinning.
Choices: Pay 2 Gold: 3 Tiny Imps stand up at the back and walk away from you; defeat all 3 before they leave the board, Gain a random item | Leave
What it is there: A small shrine with an imp on top. Activating it lets out five non-aggressive Tiny Imps that run away; kill all five in time and an item appears.
Why it fits: A chase you pay for: the reward only comes if you catch them all before they're gone.
Needs: new: bodies that walk away and leave the board

Name: Roulette Chamber
Description: A glass chamber with a lever, and something different inside every second.
Choices: Pay 2 Gold: three pieces flash past one at a time; take one as it passes, or the last is yours | Leave
What it is there: Pay to start it: items cycle in the chamber, faster and faster, and you stop it on the one showing; leave it too long and it picks for you.
Why it fits: Picking a prize as it flashes past is a small skill test that fits an object.
Needs: new: an offer taken or passed one piece at a time

Name: Embedded Blade
Description: The hilt of a blade protrudes from a massive rock. No one would embed an ordinary weapon in stone.
Choices: Pull (again): 1 time in 3, Gain a random Weapon and the stone is empty; otherwise lose 1 Health | Leave
What it is there: An overworld encounter, a Strength check with five rolls that rewards a Blade weapon, and can be attempted until it succeeds.
Why it fits: A sword in a stone you can keep trying, which is exactly what an object with a repeat is for.

Name: Shrine of Tyr
Description: A shrine to Tyr, the Peacekeeper. III is scratched into the wall behind it.
Choices: Offer 3 Gold: Gain a random Buff | Offer 9 Gold: Gain a random Weapon | Offer 4 Gold: a random Buff or a random Debuff | Leave (three gifts, then it goes quiet)
What it is there: Shrines to mechanical gods take scrap offerings, up to three gifts each. Tyr, the Peacekeeper, wants multiples of 3 (shown in Roman numerals in the background); any other amount gets a random outcome, good or bad.
Why it fits: A shrine with a lucky number: pay it right and it gives, pay it wrong and it rolls the dice.
Builds on: gain_buff, gain_item (weapon), the objects sheet Limit column

Name: Revenant Station
Description: A pedestal under a glass dome, and a scanner waiting to read you.
Choices: Be scanned: the next time you would drop to 0 Health this run, come back at full Health instead | Leave
What it is there: A room that scans you on its pedestal and rebuilds you once when you are destroyed, items and all. It looks like Super Metroid's title screen.
Why it fits: A checkpoint you step on in advance, which is how an extra life reads as a place.
Builds on: Dio's Best Friend (item candidate), the same revive
Needs: new: a revive for the player
Clones: Reconstructor (Returnal): you pay 6 Ether to power it, and if you die you are rebuilt there with your inventory, but the region's boss is back at full health

Name: The Traitor
Description: A moleman with his back to the tunnel, keeping an eye out for his own kind.
Choices: Shelf of three face-down pieces: you see what you bought after you pay
What it is there: A moleman who betrayed his own kind to help you, in the Buried City. He sells up to three items, not revealed until bought.
Why it fits: A shop whose stock you can't see until you've paid: a different kind of shelf.
Needs: new: face-down shop stock

Name: Distress Call
Goal: Save a hostage caught in the line of fire
Description: Two civilians pinned down, and the turrets already turning.
What it is there: A zone with up to two Hostages in the line of fire of turrets; save them and each pays out by type (a heal, 20 Sera, or an artifact).
Why it fits: Getting someone out of the line of fire is a goal most action games can offer.

Name: Tree
Description: A tree with 2 Health stands on the board. Destroy it and a random food piece drops
What it is there: Trees grow in the arena; hitting one down drops consumables. The Tree item makes more spawn, Pocket Factory turns a felled tree into a turret, and the Lootworm pet cuts them down.
Why it fits: A thing on the board worth spending a hit on, which feeds the food family (9 live pieces).

Name: Clone Machine
Description: A booth that copies whatever you put in it, for a price. It works three times, then never again.
Choices: Clone an item: pay its price +1 Gold, and get an exact copy | Clone yourself: pay 5 Gold, and a copy of you fights beside you next game | Leave
What it is there: A usable object in casinos, labs and shops: 'Clone Self' gives you an aligned copy of your class, 'Clone Item' costs about 25% more than buying it and gives an exact duplicate. Items can be cloned only 3 times a run.
Why it fits: Copying is a live verb (copy_item) with nowhere to stand; this is that, as a machine with a price.

Name: Well
Description: An old well. People say it grants luck, for the right coin.
Choices: Throw in 1 Gold: nothing happens | Throw in 3 Gold: Gain +1 Luck for your next game | Leave
What it is there: Throw in $1 and nothing happens; throw in $30 and you are Feelin' Lucky for 60 seconds (better loot, more crits). One go per well; destroying it makes you Feelin' Unlucky.
Why it fits: A wishing well whose cheap option is a joke on the player. NetHack's Fountain (a candidate) is about quaffing and dipping, not paying.

Name: Killer Plant
Description: Can't be moved. Each turn it bites whatever stands next to it, enemy or you, for 1
What it is there: A hazard in Park and Uptown greenhouses: it bites anyone within about 2 tiles for 10. NPCs know to avoid it, and it is hard to kill up close.
Why it fits: A hazard that doesn't take sides; pushing enemies into its reach is the play.

Name: Blood Altar
Description: A stained altar beside a sealed door. Others have bled here before you.
Choices: Bleed on it: Lose 1 Health and Gain +1 Small Chest; 1 time in 2 you also gain a random curse | Leave
What it is there: Interacting with it opens a door but deals 1 damage, and can give Blood infection, Slow metabolism, Tetanus or Unknown virus: 'Contaminated blood may have been spilled by some of the sacrificed.'
Why it fits: A blood price with a second, hidden cost; NetHack's Altar (a candidate) is about praying and sacrifice, not bleeding.

Name: Healing Statue
Description: A statue of the Templar God. Pray, and it mends you, for a little faith.
Choices: Pray: pay 1 Gold, Gain +2 Health. The fifth time you pray at one in a run, also Gain +2 Max Health | Leave
What it is there: Restores two pips of health for about 20 Faith; found before boss rooms and in every Crusaders' Haven. Using them 5 times in one life grants the Cherished by God blessing.
Why it fits: A healing stop that rewards coming back to it, which events don't do yet.
Needs: new: an object that counts uses across a run

Name: Oil Slick
Description: Enemies in it move 1 slower. If Fire touches it, every Oil Slick square connected to it becomes Fire
What it is there: A trap in the Purged Hamlet: oil or mud that slows you; a Beast Tamer's molotov sets it ablaze, and standing in it too long gives Pulmonary lesion.
Why it fits: Tiles are thin (2 live), and this one plugs into the Fire tile: lay it, then light it.

Name: Claw Machine
Description: A glass case piled with prizes, and a claw that never quite holds on.
Choices: Play: pay 2 Gold and roll: 1 in 3 you grab a random Rare item, 1 in 3 nothing, 1 in 3 the claw hits a bomb and you take 1 Damage | Leave
What it is there: A special room: 10 coins a try, the arm sweeps left to right with two bombs below it, and you press to drop the claw. Touch a bomb and the attempt is over; reach the top and you keep the prize.
Why it fits: The arcade objects are 2 live (both Isaac's donation machines); a claw machine is the arcade game everyone has lost money to.

Name: Well of Transmutation
Description: A magic well. Whatever you drop in comes back as something else.
Choices: Drop in a piece: it becomes a random piece of the same kind (an item stays an item). The well is then dry | Leave
What it is there: One of three Magic Wells (Health, Awareness, Transmutation); every well is beneficial and works once, so 'consider your options carefully' before using it.
Why it fits: Transmute is one of the five verbs, and nothing on the map lets you transmute on purpose. A one-shot well is the decision the wiki describes.

Name: Healing Springs
Description: Warm springs in the hills. A good place to rest, if your mind is steady.
Choices: Rest: Gain +3 Health. If you are below half Health, 1 in 3 you also gain a random curse | Leave
What it is there: A resting location: one rest lasts 5 days and restores 40 Sanity and heals injuries; resting under 30 Sanity can trigger bad events, and Acrophobia can start here.
Why it fits: A rest stop with a catch for the desperate: the healthier you arrive, the safer it is.

Name: Stone Circle
Description: A ring of standing stones, carved with old directions. You can read one line before the light goes.
Choices: Read of ruins: every Event game on the map is revealed | Read of settlements: every Shop is revealed | Read of danger: every Champion is revealed | Leave
What it is there: Decipher the inscriptions to reveal one of four kinds of location across the map: ruins, settlements, camp points or caves. Only one can be chosen.
Why it fits: NetHack's Scroll of Magic Mapping (a candidate) reveals everything; this makes you choose what to know.
Needs: new: revealing one kind of node

Name: Baz
Description: A frog merchant with nine pieces on his blanket, now and then some of them half price.
Choices: Shelf as usual, a few pieces on sale at half price | Give him a Tasty Fly: everything is half price | Sell him up to 3 pieces at half their price
What it is there: The Dungeon Shop: Baz carries 9 items at full price, sometimes some on sale for half. You can sell him up to 3 of your own items each visit; give him the Tasty Fly and everything is sold at the sale price.
Why it fits: Named shopkeepers are planned (spec §14.5). Baz's gift makes a trade with the shopkeeper, not only with the shelf.
Needs: new: selling to a shop

Name: Shrine of Glass
Description: A shrine of clear glass. Bump into it, and everything you carry turns to glass.
Choices: Bump it: every weapon you carry Stuns double, and breaks the first time you take damage | Leave
What it is there: A shrine that replaces your shovel, weapon, armour, headwear, torch and boots with glass versions; glass equipment breaks when you are hit. Left alone, it drops Glass Armor.
Why it fits: Power that shatters: a run-changing choice with the cost spelled out.
Needs: new: weapons that break on damage

Name: Shrine of War
Description: A shrine hung with weapons. It gives freely, and promises you a harder fight for it.
Choices: Bump it: Gain a random Rare item. From now on every enemy comes as its hardest kind | Leave
What it is there: Gives a Circlet of Telepathy or Monocle and a Scroll of Gigantism, then all future monsters spawn as their hardest versions (white skeletons become black ones). Left alone, it drops the Ring of War.
Why it fits: A gift that raises the difficulty for the rest of the run.
Needs: new: enemies spawning a tier up

Name: Bounce Trap
Description: Whatever enters it is pushed 1 square the way its arrow points
What it is there: A trap that bounces the victim one tile in the direction of its arrow; blank ones bounce you one extra tile the way you were going, and in Zone 3 some rotate every beat. Monsters trigger them too.
Why it fits: Tiles are thin (2 live), and this one turns Push into a combo: shove an enemy onto it and it goes further.

Name: Gladiator Camp
Goal: Win three arena fights in a row, each harder than the last
What it is there: A location with a market that sells slaves and no resting; its Arena pits you against a Bandit Chief, each repeat harder, for a Rare or Legendary item and batteries every win.
Why it fits: Arenas and gauntlets are everywhere (Gungeon's Winchester, Hades' trials, fighting-game survival modes). Locations are thin (2 live).

Name: Contact Light
Goal: Collect 4 keys or keycards in one level
What it is there: The final stage, 'Risk of Rain', is the crashed UES freighter Contact Light. Four Keycards, carried by marked enemies and found in gold containers, open all its locked doors.
Why it fits: Keycard hunts close many games (Doom, System Shock, Gungeon's keys). Locations are thin (2 live), and this one pays the scarcest thing, a Key.

Name: Tower of Sisyphus
Goal: Keep playing a game's endless mode past where its story ends
What it is there: Returnal's endless mode (the Ascension DLC): an ever-shifting tower climbed until you die, scoring as you go, with Algos every 20 rooms.
Why it fits: Endless modes are everywhere (Vampire Survivors, Isaac's Greed, Hades' Heat). Locations are thin (2 live).

Name: Malignant Chest
Description: A chest wrapped in pink, pulsing growth.
Choices: Open it: Gain a random piece, and 1 in 2 you get a random curse | Leave it
What it is there: Malignant containers and items carry a chance of a Suit Malfunction when you take them; a Malfunction stays until its task is done.
Why it fits: A gamble that reads at a glance: free loot with a visible infection. Objects are thin (2 live), and it hands out curses, which few things do.

Name: Tony
Description: A massive crab behind the counter. His shop changes with the island it stands on.
Choices: Shelf of perks, weapon mods and hearts | Provoke him: he fights you (a boss stands up on the board)
What it is there: Tony the shopkeeper, a massive crab who owns the shop island (perks, grenade and weapon mods, hearts, the Enhancement Totem). His shop reflects the biome, and the developer has said he will be a secret boss when provoked.
Why it fits: No shopkeeper is authored yet, and the 'provoke the shopkeeper' fight is a genre joke (Spelunky, Isaac's Greed). The fight is planned in his game, not released, so it's marked check.

Name: Health Totem
Description: A monolith with a heart carved into it. It works once.
Choices: Touch it: 1 in 2 your Max Health doubles, otherwise it halves | Leave
What it is there: One of the island totems: interacting has a 50% chance to double or halve your max health. Its neighbours: the Gold Totem (a legendary item for 66% of max health) and the Fuse Totem (an item, then it explodes).
Why it fits: A coin flip on the one stat you can't buy back, and nothing to think about but nerve. Objects are thin (2 live).

Name: Bundit Camp
Goal: Clear an enemy camp of every enemy, the ones that wandered off included
What it is there: Enemy camps are scattered over every biome, marked by a flag; all of a camp's enemies (marked pink) must die, even those that roam away, before its loot drops (seeds, roses, pickaxes, a turret, an upgrade).
Why it fits: Clearing an outpost to the last straggler is in Far Cry, Assassin's Creed and most open-world games. Locations are thin (2 live). Brogue's Goblin Warren asks for a war band and its leader; this asks for every last member, wherever it wandered.

Name: Minotaur Maze
Goal: Find the way out of a maze while something hunts you
What it is there: The Minotaur, the Baron's pet, always spawns in the Minotaur Maze; on its floors it arrives after 2:30 and barrels at the nearest player, breaking walls, and a Daedalus Shrine helps you escape.
Why it fits: A labyrinth with something in it is as old as the myth and turns up everywhere (Pac-Man, Amnesia, Alien: Isolation's corridors). Locations are thin (2 live).

Name: Teleportation Trap
Description: A body that enters this tile is teleported to a random empty square
What it is there: A gadget trap you arm on walls, the ground, doors or chests: it teleports its target to a random spot on the level, or to the trap itself if you tune it with a lockpick.
Why it fits: A tile that scatters the board's front line, for you or against you. Tiles are thin (2 live), and the wands' Teleportation already moves single bodies.

Name: Sunshine Island
Goal: Shake off a pursuer by fleeing somewhere it can't follow
What it is there: A Map's Edge destination in the Exile legacy: 'I find a room above the harbor. When my Foe comes, I'll wait for him out on the cliffs.' Your allies can't follow, but neither can lesser reckoners: Safety from Pursuit.
Why it fits: Losing a pursuer (GTA's wanted level, Alien: Isolation, Mr. X) is a goal many games host. Locations are thin (2 live).

Name: ATM
Goal: Pay off a debt before its deadline
What it is there: The ATM is where coins are deposited to repay the Debt; it shows the rounds left in the deadline, the interest and the amount owed. Miss a deadline and the Announcer begins the Death Countdown.
Why it fits: Debts with a due date (Animal Crossing's loan, Stardew's community fund, Lethal Company's quota) are a common shape, and paying one off is a real goal. Locations are thin (2 live).

Name: Cordelia
Description: The daughter of the house, behind the counter, with a line for every item she sells.
Choices: Shelf as usual | Buy anything: she tells you a story about it (no effect)
What it is there: The shopkeeper NPC: Cordelia Valentine sells the mansion's items, each with its own shopkeeper quote ('Grandpa's in there!' for the Ancient Urn). Her own curse, Curse of the Daughter, lowers shop prices.
Why it fits: No shopkeeper is authored yet, and hers is a voice the shop panel can carry: one line per piece.
Needs: new: a quote per piece in the shop

Name: Bancho Sushi
Goal: Serve customers through a whole shift
What it is there: The sushi bar financed by Cobra and run by Bancho: Dave catches the fish by day and serves tables by night, and the restaurant's rating draws more customers.
Why it fits: Restaurant and shop shifts are a genre of their own (Overcooked, Cook, Serve, Delicious!, Moonlighter, Coffee Talk) and turn up as minigames everywhere. Locations are thin (2 live).

Name: Pot
Description: A light blue ceramic pot, the kind found in every corner of Tasos.
Choices: Smash it: a random pickup (Gold, Health, a gem); 1 in 4 a Slither snake jumps out and stands up on the board | Throw it at an enemy: Stun 1 to a random enemy | Leave it
What it is there: Pots hold ammo, glass tools, health, magic, gems and Tasian gold; they can be picked up and thrown at enemies, and in dungeons some are traps housing Slithers.
Why it fits: Smashing pots is the Zelda habit every adventure game inherited. Objects are thin (2 live), and this one is a small gamble.

Name: The Crow
Description: A crow behind the counter who wants your worst things, and pays for them.
Choices: Shelf as usual | Trade her a cursed piece from your pack: take a random piece in exchange, of a better rarity the worse the curse was | Leave
What it is there: In the shop, the Crow drops items in exchange for the artifacts you bring her: harmful pieces you carry at a cost, each with a risk value, the riskier the better the trade.
Why it fits: No shopkeeper is authored yet, and she buys curses, which gives the cursed pieces (Infected Bandages, Punish Ball, Evil Deal) a way out.
Needs: new: trading a piece to a shop

Name: Glass Shrine
Description: A shrine of clear glass, with a boss you've already beaten caught inside it.
Choices: Break it: the last boss you beat stands up again on your next board, already hurt; beat it again for its chest | Leave it
What it is there: One of the Saint Shrines: refight a previously beaten boss; with its Curio and Blessing equipped, the boss starts the refight with 10 damage sealed on it, and the player is hexed.
Why it fits: A rematch for a second reward, the boss-rush idea in one choice. Objects are thin (2 live).

Name: Statue of Kismet
Description: A stone statue of a man in a mask, holding out two gifts.
Choices: Take one: choose one of two random pieces | Grab both: take both, and an extra enemy stands up on your next board | Leave
What it is there: Statues of Kismet offer a choice of two rewards; dash fast enough and you take both, which brings more elite enemies, and doing it three times locks every other statue that run. Kismet turned to stone wearing a mask he made to become a spirit, out of greed.
Why it fits: A greed choice told through its own legend. Objects with a choice are still few among the live ones.

Name: Homing Spike Block
Description: Can't be destroyed. Each turn it slides one square toward you, and deals 1 damage to any body it slides into.
What it is there: A trap the dead can possess: 'This spiked slab grinds across the floor, drawn towards living flesh.' Its siblings, the Spike Block Trap and the Greater Spike Block, slide on fixed tracks.
Why it fits: The only unit that moves: it hunts you, and anything in its path, so the board's bodies become its shield or its victims.
Needs: new: a unit that moves

Name: Exchange Room
Description: A small room with two counters, one for keys and one for bombs.
Choices: Trade 1 Key for 1 Bomb | Trade 1 Bomb for 1 Key | Leave
What it is there: A dreamscape room that lets Cassidy exchange keys and bombs. 'I'm a demolitionist, not a rogue.'
Why it fits: Keys and Bombs are both live counters, and nothing yet trades one for the other.

Name: Deity Statue
Description: A statue of one of the island's gods, a dish of coins at its feet. It remembers who passes it by.
Choices: Donate 1 Gold: the god is pleased, and every enemy of your next game is Stunned 1 at its start | Walk past: the god is offended, and one more body stands up at the start of your next game
What it is there: Each of the seven deities has statues across the island that take coin donations. Pleased gods bless chests with their coins or curse enemies weaker; ignored, enraged gods make enemies far stronger.
Why it fits: An object with no free option: leaving costs as well, which none of the live objects do.

Name: Green Leaf
Description: A body that steps on it is moved to another Green Leaf on the board. With only one leaf, nothing happens.
What it is there: An obstacle: 'Teleports any character that steps on it to a random Green Leaf. If the room has only 1 leaf, nothing happens.'
Why it fits: Paired tiles that move bodies give Push and the swap weapons a board to play on.
Needs: new: a tile that teleports

Name: Campfire
Description: A fire between stages, with a blacksmith's anvil beside it.
Choices: Rest: Gain +2 Health | Reforge: two pieces from your pack melt into one random piece, a rarity higher than the better of them | Leave
What it is there: Campfires sit between stages: they restore health and revive fallen allies, items can be baked or burnt there, and the blacksmith reforges 2 items into a new one, possibly of a higher tier.
Why it fits: A rest stop with a choice; two pieces for one better one is a trade the pack has no other way to make.
Needs: new: merging two pieces

Name: Huginn
Description: A giant armless chicken with a halo, dancing to whistled punk. He rewards regulars.
Choices: Shelf of three pieces | Every 5 Gold you have spent with Huginn this run opens one more slot on his shelf | Leave
What it is there: Huginn's Shop is BPM's merchant: at first only three items can be bought, and more open up as gold is spent and added to Huginn's Loyalty Card. The same tune plays in it on every floor.
Why it fits: A shopkeeper with a loyalty card: shopping in one place pays. No shopkeeper is live yet.
Needs: new: a shelf that grows with spending

Name: Arlan
Description: A shopkeeper with a wooden sign over the counter, and strong feelings about the sign.
Choices: Shelf as usual; a reroll costs 1 Gold, doubling each time | Smash the sign: Gain 1 Gold. Arlan is furious, and it changes nothing | Leave
What it is there: Arlan's shops sell relics and skills for coins; rerolls start at 25 coins and double, to 300. Every shop has a sign that drops 5-10 coins when broken; Arlan gets angry, but it is purely for show and he comes back later in the run.
Why it fits: A shopkeeper with a joke built in: vandalism that pays a little and costs nothing but his temper.

Name: Offering Pit
Description: A pit full of green slime that gives back what you feed it, changed.
Choices: Feed it up to 4 pieces from your pack: each comes back as a random piece of the same rarity | Leave
What it is there: The ??? Shop: a room where you give a green slime pit up to 4 relics or skills in exchange for a new set of the same rarity.
Why it fits: A reroll for the pack itself, at no price but certainty.
Needs: new: swapping pieces for others of their rarity
Clones: Jester (Die in the Dungeon): a special event that rerolls three or ALL of your dice at once, of any kind

Name: Repair Gel
Description: At the end of each game it stands on the board, Gain +1 Health. If anything destroys it, take 1 Damage.
What it is there: A strategic tile: 'Repairs 4 hull to units in 3 tiles range. Upon destruction, adds +2 Internal Damage.'
Why it fits: A unit worth guarding: the bombs and the push weapons have a reason to mind where they land.
